results.summary_before: This design is an 8-bit pseudo-random number generator built from four Fibonacci maximum-length LFSRs of 9, 10, 11 and 13 bits, whose outputs are XOR-combined. The chip clock is divided by 14 cascaded divide-by-two stages, giving a total division of 16384, so a 10 kHz clock yields about 0.61 Hz for the LFSRs. The eight random bits appear on the eight output pins and can be observed with a 7-segment LED display, an oscilloscope or a logic analyzer. A 7-segment LED display is recommended as external hardware, and the design is notable for using relatively prime LFSR lengths to reduce correlation.
